events.title: US midterm elections — Democrats win control of Congress
events.why_it_matters: Democratic control of both chambers blocks Trump's legislative agenda but may reduce tariff-escalation risk, reshaping the policy backdrop for all sectors.
events.what_to_watch: Lame-duck session must-pass bills and whether Trump pivots to executive action.

events.title: US October employment report — +165k vs +60k consensus
events.why_it_matters: A much stronger-than-expected payrolls print keeps the Fed on a hawkish path and raises the bar for a December pause, with rate-sensitive sectors most exposed.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the strength persists into the November report and how it interacts with CPI.

events.title: USTR extends Section 301 exclusions to January 9, 2027
events.why_it_matters: The last-minute extension averts a punitive tariff snap-back on 178 industrial categories, removing a near-term cost shock for manufacturers and retailers.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the two-month extension becomes a bridge to a broader truce or just delays the cliff to January.

events.title: China October CPI 0.7% y/y, PPI 5.7% y/y
events.why_it_matters: CPI missed consensus and core inflation softened, reinforcing deflation fears and expectations for additional stimulus, while the PPI-CPI scissors gap widens margin pressure downstream.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Beijing responds with fresh consumption support at the December politburo meeting.

events.title: BOJ October meeting minutes — hawkish, December hike signal
events.why_it_matters: Minutes confirm policymakers favour raising rates as inflation nears 2%, cementing expectations for a December hike to 1.5% and supporting the yen at the margin.
events.what_to_watch: Governor Ueda's next public remarks and the December 18-19 BOJ meeting.

events.title: White House postpones Fed Governor Cook removal hearing to December 14
events.why_it_matters: The delay reduces immediate Fed-independence risk but keeps a cloud over monetary-policy governance and the December FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Cook's lawyers agree to participate and whether the hearing actually proceeds on December 14.

events.title: OPEC+ maintains December output at September levels; next meeting November 29
events.why_it_matters: The decision to hold output steady removes a near-term supply shock but leaves the market sensitive to the November 29 meeting and demand signals from China.
events.what_to_watch: Compliance with quotas and whether the group signals any change for Q1 2027.

events.title: PBOC raises FX deposit reserve ratio to 6% effective November 15
events.why_it_matters: The 200bp hike tightens onshore FX liquidity and signals Beijing's discomfort with rapid yuan depreciation, with spillovers to Asian currencies and exporters.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the yuan stabilises or the PBOC follows with further macro-prudential measures.

events.title: Bank of England raises Bank Rate 25bp to 4.00%
events.why_it_matters: The first hike since 2023 and an 8-1 vote signals a hawkish tilt, though the market is pricing it as a one-and-done insurance move.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the BoE signals another hike at the December meeting.

events.title: Korea Supreme Court upholds KFTC penalty against Broadcom
events.why_it_matters: The ruling exhausts Broadcom's judicial options in Korea and reinforces antitrust scrutiny of long-term supply contracts in semiconductors.
events.what_to_watch: Read-across to other jurisdictions and whether Broadcom adjusts its Korean contracting practices.

events.title: Supreme Court conference on Nielsen antitrust petition (November 13)
events.why_it_matters: The justices will consider whether to hear Nielsen's challenge to an antitrust injunction, with potential read-across to platform and data-pricing regulation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Court grants certiorari and sets a briefing schedule.

events.title: Port strikes at LA/Long Beach and across Europe disrupt supply chains
events.why_it_matters: Labour stoppages at major gateways are causing loading delays and cargo diversion, raising freight costs and threatening holiday-season inventory.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the LA/Long Beach watchmen strike is averted and how long European port disruptions persist.

events.title: Typhoon Cempaka tracks toward Philippines and Taiwan
events.why_it_matters: The storm threatens semiconductor and electronics production hubs, with potential short-term supply disruptions.
events.what_to_watch: Taiwan and Philippines landfall timing and any fab or port closures.

events.title: Taiwan stocks rally 6% as stabilisation fund and chipmakers rebound
events.why_it_matters: The rally in TSMC and MediaTek signals a partial recovery in AI/semiconductor sentiment after last week's selloff, with read-across to global tech.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the bounce is sustained or fades into Nvidia earnings on November 17.

events.title: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris on Ukraine and Iran
events.why_it_matters: The meeting may produce coordinated pressure on Russia and Iran, with implications for oil and sanctions regimes.
events.what_to_watch: Any joint statement on Ukraine peace talks or new Iran measures.

events.title: Russia-US-Ukraine trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi (November 10-11)
events.why_it_matters: Any progress toward a ceasefire would weigh on energy prices and European risk assets; failure keeps the war premium intact.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a joint statement or framework is announced.

events.title: European Political Community summit in Dublin (November 12)
events.why_it_matters: Over 50 European leaders meet to discuss security and Ukraine, with potential signals on defence spending and energy policy.
events.what_to_watch: Whether new defence or energy initiatives are announced.

events.title: Trump threatens tariffs up to 300% on companies not manufacturing in US
events.why_it_matters: Despite the midterm loss, Trump is doubling down on tariff threats, keeping policy uncertainty elevated for importers and multinationals.
events.what_to_watch: Whether any of the threatened measures are formalised in the next 1-2 weeks.

events.title: US Treasury sanctions eight Canadian firms over Iran ties
events.why_it_matters: The sanctions expand the Iran pressure campaign and signal continued aggressive enforcement, with spillovers to currency-exchange and oil-trading networks.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Iran retaliates or further designations follow.

events.title: US October CPI (November 10) — consensus +0.3% m/m
events.why_it_matters: The single most important data point before the December FOMC; an upside surprise would cement a hike, while a downside print could revive pause hopes. Note BLS will not publish y/y figures due to the shutdown.
events.what_to_watch: Core m/m and the truncated detail; market reaction in rates and tech.

events.title: US October PPI (November 13) — consensus +0.4% m/m, 6.6% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline inflation after September's upside surprise; a hot print would reinforce the higher-for-longer narrative and pressure margins.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI and services components.

events.title: FOMC minutes of the October 27-28 meeting (November 18)
events.why_it_matters: Markets will parse the minutes for the breadth of the hawkish hold and any explicit December guidance.
events.what_to_watch: Language on 'restrictive' policy and the balance of risks.

events.title: US October retail sales (November 17)
events.why_it_matters: Consumer resilience is the last pillar supporting the hawkish Fed; a soft print would raise growth concerns into the holiday season.
events.what_to_watch: Control group and discretionary categories.

events.title: US October housing starts (November 18)
events.why_it_matters: Housing is the most rate-sensitive sector; a weak print would confirm the toll of higher mortgage rates.
events.what_to_watch: Single-family starts and permits.

events.title: China October trade data (November 10)
events.why_it_matters: Exports have been front-running tariff deadlines; the data will show whether momentum is fading as the truce holds.
events.what_to_watch: Export growth to the US and EU, and any signs of pre-shipment distortion.

events.title: China October retail sales and industrial production (November 16)
events.why_it_matters: Retail sales growth near 1% and slowing IP would confirm weak domestic demand and reinforce stimulus expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Retail sales y/y and whether IP holds above 5%.

events.title: Nvidia Q3 FY2027 earnings (November 17)
events.why_it_matters: The bellwether for the entire AI trade; after a 9.3% one-day drop on November 5, guidance will determine whether the selloff deepens or reverses.
events.what_to_watch: Data-center revenue, Q4 guidance, and commentary on supply constraints.

events.title: Anthropic IPO — roadshow expected week of November 16
events.why_it_matters: The largest AI IPO to date, with a targeted valuation of $1.25-1.75 trillion; a successful listing would revive risk appetite, while a stumble would amplify the tech selloff.
events.what_to_watch: Final price range, demand during the roadshow, and first-day trading.

events.title: Cisco Q1 FY2027 earnings (November 12)
events.why_it_matters: Cisco is a barometer for networking and AI infrastructure demand; options price an 8% swing, and a weak guide could hit the broader tech complex.
events.what_to_watch: AI order commentary and FY27 guidance.

events.title: Applied Materials Q4 FY2026 earnings (November 12)
events.why_it_matters: Results are expected to match guidance; the real focus is the 2027 outlook, which will signal the durability of the semiconductor capex cycle.
events.what_to_watch: 2027 revenue and EPS guidance, and China exposure.

events.title: Walt Disney Q4 FY2026 earnings (November 17)
events.why_it_matters: Disney's streaming profitability and parks demand are key tests for the media and consumer discretionary sectors.
events.what_to_watch: Direct-to-consumer margins and parks revenue guidance.

events.title: Home Depot Q3 2026 earnings (November 17)
events.why_it_matters: A read on housing turnover and renovation demand amid elevated mortgage rates.
events.what_to_watch: Comparable sales and pro-customer demand.

events.title: Walmart Q3 FY2027 earnings (November 19)
events.why_it_matters: The largest US retailer is the best real-time read on consumer health and holiday-season inventory; guidance will move the whole retail sector.
events.what_to_watch: US comp sales, e-commerce growth, and margin commentary.

events.title: Target Q3 2026 earnings (November 18)
events.why_it_matters: Target's discretionary mix makes it a purer read on consumer stress than Walmart; a weak print would reinforce the slowdown narrative.
events.what_to_watch: Traffic, markdowns, and digital sales.

events.title: Lame-duck Congress returns; government funding deadline December 11
events.why_it_matters: The Republican-held chambers must avert a shutdown before Democrats take control in January, with must-pass defence and farm bills also on the agenda.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a stopgap is passed or a shutdown fight emerges in early December.

top_risks: US October CPI on November 10 surprises to the upside, cementing a December Fed hike and triggering a broad risk-off move, especially in tech and rate-sensitive sectors.
Nvidia's November 17 earnings disappoint or guide down, deepening the AI-led selloff that began in early November.
Anthropic's IPO prices poorly or trades below range, signalling investor fatigue with mega-cap AI valuations and weighing on the entire technology complex.
The December 11 government funding deadline collapses into a shutdown, hitting consumer confidence and delaying data releases.
Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi fail to produce any de-escalation, keeping energy prices elevated and European risk premia wide.
top_opportunities: A soft US CPI print on November 10 could revive hopes of a Fed pause, sparking a relief rally in growth and rate-sensitive names.
Section 301 extension removes a near-term tariff cliff for industrial and tech importers, supporting margins into year-end.
China stimulus expectations are rising after weak October CPI; any new consumption support would lift China-exposed consumer and industrial names.
A successful Anthropic IPO could restore risk appetite for AI and technology, reversing part of November's selloff.
Walmart and Target earnings may show consumer resilience, providing a positive catalyst for the retail sector ahead of the holiday season.
summary: Markets enter the week with a hawkish Fed on hold, strong October payrolls, and critical inflation data and mega-cap AI earnings in the next fortnight. The main tension is between a market pricing a December hike and data that could force a pause, while the Section 301 cliff has been deferred and the AI trade remains fragile after Nvidia's sharp drawdown. Key swing factors are US CPI on November 10, Nvidia's November 17 earnings, and the Anthropic IPO.
